title: Traffic oscillation dampening and staged upgrade policy
creator: Ava Chen
description: Define and implement a staged upgrade policy that prevents oscillating traffic ramps during canary rollouts. The goal is to add a dampening layer on top of weighted canaries and percent ramps so that transient metric spikes don't cause rapid back-and-forth rollbacks or excessive throttling. This work spans routing rules, feature-flag integration, and an orchestrator-side damping controller that enforces cool-down windows and stabilization windows per cohort.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Rollouts support a configurable stabilization window (default 10 minutes) and dampening factor to limit upward/downward delta to <= 20% per step.
A2: Canary can be configured with a ttl-based cool-down that blocks repeated rollbacks/re-promotions within 30 minutes per cohort.
A3: System exposes gating metrics and decisions in Console rollouts UI (traffic delta, reason codes, history of rollbacks).
A4: Automated mitigations (traffic freeze, failover to fallback model, throttled downgrade) trigger when SLO breach conditions persist for > 2 consecutive windows.
A5: Integration tests simulate oscillation scenarios and show reduced oscillation events by >= 80% compared to baseline policy.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature-flag rollout to internal org + smoke tests (0-1%)
Phase 1: Weighted canary ramp with dampening: 1% -> 3% -> 6% -> 12% (each step min 10m stabilization, max delta capped to 2x previous share)
Phase 2: Gradual promotion to 25% -> 50% with cohort-aware cool-downs and health checks
Phase 3: Final promotion to 100% with post-promotion monitoring and optional LTS pinning
Abort conditions: metric breach across error-rate OR p95 latency OR token-throughput with severity thresholds documented below
metrics_gates: Primary gates: error_rate_inference > 0.8% sustained for 5m triggers immediate rollback action
Latency gate: p95_latency increase > 35% vs baseline sustained for two consecutive stabilization windows triggers throttled rollback (freeze then 50% backoff)
Quality gate: BLEU/semantic similarity regressions on held eval set > 4% require manual approval
Traffic safety gate: downstream queue saturation > 70% occupancy for two windows will shift traffic to fallback model variant
mitigation_playbook: 1) Automatic: dampening controller reduces next-step delta by configured factor (default 0.5) and opens cool-down timer
2) Automatic: if persistent breach > 20m, orchestrator routes new traffic to last-known-good deployment and marks cohort as quarantined
3) Manual: on-call runbook with commands to pin LTS channel, force-promote or force-rollback via CLI, and to rotate model variant
4) Post-incident: collect traces, KV cache state, batching histograms, and artifact links for postmortem
testing_plan: Unit tests: dampening math, timer state transitions, and idempotent rollback commands
Integration: e2e with routing layer + feature flag toggles in staging cluster, synthetic error injection to validate auto-mitigation
Chaos: scheduled network latency injection and burst traffic simulation to verify oscillation dampening under stress
Perf: ensure no >5% added latency from controller decision path in p95 on small workloads
implementation_notes: Controller will live as a stateless operator with a small state store (TTL entries keyed by cohort) — prefer existing rollout metadata store; avoid adding another persistent system unless needed
Traffic deltas computed using smoothed exponential moving average over last 3 windows to avoid reacting to single-window spikes
Expose knobs in Console: stabilization_window, dampening_factor, max_step_delta, cohort_cooldown_minutes
We will reuse existing rollout history schema but extend it with "reason_code" and "dampening_applied" flags (UI requires minimal change)
Estimate bulk of infra work 3 dev-weeks, UI + tests 1.5 dev-weeks
risk_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: stricter dampening reduces risk of oscillation but slows recovery for legitimate fixes; choose conservative defaults and make aggressive defaults opt-in
Risk: hidden state and TTL bugs could prevent expected re-promotions; mitigate via thorough integration tests and canary on internal org
Operational cost: slightly longer time-to-100% for fixes—documented as acceptable to reduce user-facing thrash
observability_and_alerting: Dashboard: Rollout timeline per cohort with applied dampening factor, health metrics, and rollback history (link below)
Alert: rollout_stalled_for_>30m (warning) and rollout_oscillation_detected (critical) with playbook link
Logs: controller decisions include cohort_id, desired_delta, applied_delta, reason_code, metrics_snapshot
